Dobrodzien Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dobrodzień, Poland

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Dobrodzień in the 18th century, building a wooden synagogue in 1781 and a stone one in 1848; population peaked at 233 by 1849 before westward migration to Silesia reduced it to 175 by 1896, and further antisemitism left just 14 residents by 1939, likely deported to a General Government ghetto. This cemetery, most likely founded around 1729, holds tombstones belonging to relatives of Edyta Stein (Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross, canonized by the Catholic Church). Ownership passed to the Jewish Association of Germany in 1939, then the Gestapo in 1943; destruction continued after the war, when the undertaker's quarters were demolished. In July 2001, the international 'Antyschematy' student project - coordinated by the Janusz Korczak Society of Poland with participants from Poland, Germany, and Israel - cleaned the site and built a lapidary from broken tombstone fragments while completing an inventory. The cemetery entered Poland's Register of Historical Landmarks (no. 439/88) on May 27, 1988.
